condition: blunt bungee-cord recoil injury to the left eye presenting with visible red blood layered across the lower iris in an adult man
level_rationale: A stretched bungee cord snapping into the left eye at home today and leaving visible red blood layered across the lower iris in a 37-year-old man indicates traumatic hyphema with substantial risks of occult globe rupture, acute intraocular pressure elevation, corneal blood staining, and retinal detachment requiring immediate emergency department slit-lamp examination, intraocular pressure measurement, eye shielding, and emergent ophthalmic evaluation, whereas mild left-eye watering for 1 minute at home today leaves zero traumatic or visual red flags and is appropriate for home self-care.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain adult lexical register swap (-reg) + sourced uncontracted causal belief-addition clause (-att) + Rule A same-eye brief mild watering self-care control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (37-year-old man, at home today, and a tight bungee cord hitting the left eye leaving red blood over the lower iris) with zero apostrophe contractions, an exact 13-word vs 13-word span swap, and 3 verified direct patient quotes from PMID 40395651. Keeping 'my left eye' identical in f3 avoids adding an unstated periorbital body site when f3 shifts under Rule A and Rule D to 1 minute of mild left-eye watering (level 4 ER to level 1 home self-care) with zero stated negatives.
